options.why: Wrote the marked angle itself instead of turning clockwise from north.
Turned $32^{\circ}$ from south towards the east instead of towards the west.
Measured the $32^{\circ}$ from north instead of from south.

questions.solution_text:
North to south, turning clockwise, is $180^{\circ}$, and $OA$ is a further $32^{\circ}$ clockwise.
$180^{\circ}+32^{\circ}$
$=212^{\circ}\text{T}$

questions.question_text: Convert the compass bearing $\text{S}64^{\circ}\text{E}$ to a three-figure true bearing.

options.why: Used the acute angle as the bearing, ignoring that the turn starts at south.
Added $64^{\circ}$ to $180^{\circ}$, turning towards the west instead of the east.
Subtracted $64^{\circ}$ from $360^{\circ}$, as if the turn started at north.

questions.question_text: Write the true bearing $236^{\circ}\text{T}$ as a compass bearing.

options.why: Measured the angle back from west, $270^{\circ}-236^{\circ}=34^{\circ}$, instead of forward from south.
Found $236^{\circ}-180^{\circ}=56^{\circ}$ but turned from north towards east, giving the reverse direction.
Measured $270^{\circ}-236^{\circ}=34^{\circ}$ back from west and then turned from north towards east.

questions.solution_text:
$236^{\circ}\text{T}$ lies between $180^{\circ}$ and $270^{\circ}$, so the turn is measured from south towards west.
$236^{\circ}-180^{\circ}$
$=56^{\circ}$
The compass bearing is $\text{S}56^{\circ}\text{W}$.

options.why: Used the leftover angle to the west arm, $90^{\circ}-38^{\circ}=52^{\circ}$, instead of the marked angle from north.
Gave the reverse direction, the bearing of $O$ from $A$, instead of $A$ from $O$.
Used the $90^{\circ}-38^{\circ}=52^{\circ}$ angle to the west arm and also gave the reverse direction, $O$ from $A$.

questions.solution_text:
The marked angle is measured from north and $A$ lies to the west of the north line.
The compass bearing is $\text{N}38^{\circ}\text{W}$.

questions.question_text:
The bearing of a beacon from a fishing boat is $067^{\circ}\text{T}$.
What is the bearing of the fishing boat from the beacon?

options.why: Subtracted $67^{\circ}$ from $360^{\circ}$ instead of adding $180^{\circ}$.
Subtracted $67^{\circ}$ from $180^{\circ}$ instead of adding $180^{\circ}$.
Added $90^{\circ}$, a quarter revolution, instead of $180^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
The bearing is less than $180^{\circ}$, so add $180^{\circ}$.
$67^{\circ}+180^{\circ}$
$=247^{\circ}\text{T}$

questions.question_text:
The bearing of a summit from a mountain hut is $318^{\circ}\text{T}$.
What is the bearing of the mountain hut from the summit?

options.why: Subtracted $318^{\circ}$ from $360^{\circ}$ instead of subtracting $180^{\circ}$.
Subtracted $90^{\circ}$, a quarter revolution, instead of $180^{\circ}$.
Repeated the given bearing without reversing the direction at all.

questions.solution_text:
The bearing is more than $180^{\circ}$, so subtract $180^{\circ}$.
$318^{\circ}-180^{\circ}$
$=138^{\circ}\text{T}$

questions.question_text: Which of these is written correctly as a compass bearing?

options.why: A compass bearing must start the turn at north or south, not at east or west.
The turn must be towards east or west, not back onto the north–south line.
A compass bearing turns through an acute angle, so it cannot exceed $90^{\circ}$.

questions.solution_text:
A compass bearing starts at north or south, then turns through an acute angle towards east or west.
Only $\text{S}41^{\circ}\text{W}$ meets both conditions.

questions.question_text:
The bearing of a buoy from a patrol boat is $\text{N}24^{\circ}\text{W}$.
What is the bearing of the patrol boat from the buoy, as a three-figure true bearing?

options.why: Converted $\text{N}24^{\circ}\text{W}$ to $024^{\circ}$ instead of $336^{\circ}$, then added $180^{\circ}$.
Converted the compass bearing correctly but did not reverse the direction.
Subtracted $90^{\circ}$, a quarter revolution, instead of $180^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text:
A true bearing is $a^{\circ}$, where $0^{\circ}<a^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$.
Which expression gives the true bearing of the opposite direction?

options.why: Subtracting gives a negative result whenever $a$ is less than $180$.
Reflects the direction in the north–south line instead of reversing it.
Measures the same angle anticlockwise from north instead of reversing the direction.

questions.solution_text:
The opposite direction is half a revolution away, so add or subtract $180$.
Since $a<180$, subtracting would give a negative bearing.
$a+180$

questions.question_text:
The bearing of $Q$ from $P$ is an acute angle.
The bearing of $R$ from $Q$ is a reflex angle.
Which statement about the bearing of $R$ from $P$ is correct?

options.why: The two qualitative bearing descriptions do not force an acute resultant.
The resultant could have several angle types depending on the actual directions.
A reflex intermediate bearing does not force a reflex bearing from the original point.

options.text: It could be any type of angle.

questions.solution_text: Only qualitative information is supplied about the two bearings; no numerical directions or triangle geometry are given. Different configurations can produce acute, obtuse, or reflex resultant bearings, so any type is possible.
